trust_decision.summary: Ash.Vector.new decides whether an input list's length fits the 16-bit dimension header before encoding it; at the pinned commit it encodes any length and the header silently wraps mod 65,536.

landing_point.why: The summary names Ash.Vector and the 16-bit dimension header; the only <<dim::unsigned-16>> write in the tree is here.

fix_sites.entry_point: Ash.Vector.new/1 (public API); also reached via Ash.Type.cast_input/dump_to_native/cast_stored for :vector attributes (lib/ash/type/vector.ex:41, lib/ash/type/vector.ex:69, lib/ash/type/vector.ex:83) and Ash.Vector.new(binary) (lib/ash/vector.ex:25-27)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Ash.Vector.from_binary and the %Ash.Vector{} pass-through clauses never compute a length, so a solver can argue they cannot overflow and are 'trusted, already-encoded' data from the data layer.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A vector of exactly 65,535 elements must still be accepted and round-trip through to_list; an off-by-one (>=) or a stricter cap (e.g. pgvector's 16,000 limit) breaks it. Binary input via new(binary) and the :dimensions constraint check must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: binary via Ash.Vector.new/1 (binary_to_list then the list clause)
list via Ash.Type.cast_input / dump_to_native / cast_stored for Ash.Type.Vector

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Ash.Vector.from_binary trusts the 16-bit header and never checks that the payload length matches dim, so a header/data mismatch still yields a struct whose to_list/inspect crashes
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No arithmetic happens there, so there is no overflow; it decodes data that came from storage
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 15 lines below the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Prebuilt %Ash.Vector{} structs pass through new/1, cast_stored and dump_to_native with no consistency check between dimensions and data
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The struct is assumed to have been built by new/1; validating structs is a different feature
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file plus lib/ash/type/vector.ex:64-66 and lib/ash/type/vector.ex:78-80

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cast_atomic could build a vector expression without the dimension cap check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: cast_atomic already passes the value through unvalidated, and a maintainer adding an atomic encoding path would plausibly copy the header encoding without the check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The generator produces unbounded StreamData.list_of(float) that can exceed the cap
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Generators are written for property tests and rarely mirror constructor limits

O9_family: integer overflow / truncation (narrowing an unbounded length into a 16-bit binary header field)

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir/Erlang OTP with mix (deps via hex)
O10_build.project_tests: test/type/vector_test.exs (2 tests at the pinned commit: list cast and nil)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a length guard in Ash.Type.Vector.cast_input only, which leaves the direct Ash.Vector.new/1 API and the binary path open (or use >= 65,535 and reject the legitimate limit).

out_of_scope_notes: The same v3.32.2 release fixes many other CVEs (CVE-2026-82734..82749), e.g. decimal non-finite and ci_string checks; not pursued.
unverified: The O8 routes are weak: neither involves an arithmetic overflow, and both are where-type siblings in the same file, so they are unlikely to count as uncovered routes for this advisory's property.
O1 counts Ash.Vector.new list/binary plus Ash.Type cast_input/cast_stored/dump_to_native as entry points; they all funnel into one function.
present_in_latest unknown: no latest release given.
